knowledge:
- key_parameters: method=Specifies the alignment algorithm ("ClustalW", "ClustalOmega", or "Muscle") ;; type=Specifies the sequence type ("dna", "rna", or "protein") ;; substitutionMatrix=Substitution matrix to use (ClustalOmega only supports predefined names like "BLOSUM62" or "Gonnet") ;; gapOpening=Penalty for opening a gap (not supported by ClustalOmega) ;; gapExtension=Penalty for extending a gap (not supported by ClustalOmega) ;; maxiters=Maximum number of alignment iterations ;; order=Output order of sequences ("aligned" or "input") ;; type (in msaConsensusSequence)=Consensus type, such as "upperlower" for threshold-based consensus ;; thresh (in msaConsensusSequence)=Conservation thresholds for upper/lower consensus (e.g., c(40, 20)) ;; gapVsGap (in msaConservationScore)=Score penalty/value for gap-to-gap comparisons
- alternatives: muscle=An alternative R package that only provides the MUSCLE algorithm, whereas msa provides ClustalW, ClustalOmega, and MUSCLE ;; seqinr/ape=Used downstream for distance calculation and phylogenetic tree plotting after converting the msa object
- when_to_use: Use when you need to perform multiple sequence alignment of DNA, RNA, or amino acid sequences directly within R, compute position-specific conservation scores, generate consensus sequences, or produce publication-quality alignment figures.
- pitfalls: ClustalOmega does not allow setting custom gap penalties; setting gapOpening or gapExtension will trigger a warning and have no effect ;; ClustalOmega only supports a predefined set of amino acid substitution matrices, making it unsuitable for nucleotide alignments ;; msaPrettyPrint requires a working system installation of TeX/LaTeX and the texshade.sty style file ;; Masked columns/rows are handled differently across functions: consensusMatrix returns NA for masked columns, while msaConsensusSequence represents them as '#'

workflows.name: sequence_alignment_and_pretty_printing
workflows.intent: Align amino acid or nucleotide sequences and generate a highly customizable PDF visualization of the alignment.
input: exampleAA.fasta (FASTA file containing amino acid sequences)
workflows.stages: 1. Read sequences using Biostrings ;; 2. Perform multiple sequence alignment using msa ;; 3. Print the complete alignment to the console ;; 4. Generate a pretty-printed PDF visualization using msaPrettyPrint
workflows.code:
mySequenceFile <- system.file("examples", "exampleAA.fasta", package="msa")
mySequences <- readAAStringSet(mySequenceFile)
mySequences
myFirstAlignment <- msa(mySequences)
myFirstAlignment
print(myFirstAlignment, show="complete")
msaPrettyPrint(myFirstAlignment, output="pdf", showNames="none", showLogo="none", askForOverwrite=FALSE, verbose=FALSE)

workflows.name: alignment_masking_consensus_and_conservation
workflows.intent: Apply masks to an alignment, compute consensus matrices/sequences, and calculate position-specific conservation scores.
input: exampleAA.fasta (FASTA file containing amino acid sequences)
workflows.stages: 1. Read and align sequences ;; 2. Apply a column mask using colmask and IRanges ;; 3. Retrieve the unmasked alignment ;; 4. Compute the consensus matrix ;; 5. Generate a threshold-based consensus sequence ;; 6. Calculate position-specific conservation scores using a substitution matrix
workflows.code:
mySequenceFile <- system.file("examples", "exampleAA.fasta", package="msa")
mySequences <- readAAStringSet(mySequenceFile)
myFirstAlignment <- msa(mySequences)
myMaskedAlignment <- myFirstAlignment
colM <- IRanges(start=1, end=100)
colmask(myMaskedAlignment) <- colM
myMaskedAlignment
unmasked(myMaskedAlignment)
conMat <- consensusMatrix(myMaskedAlignment)
msaConsensusSequence(myFirstAlignment, type="upperlower", thresh=c(40, 20))
library(pwalign)
data(BLOSUM62)
msaConservationScore(myFirstAlignment, BLOSUM62)

workflows.name: phylogenetic_tree_reconstruction
workflows.intent: Convert a multiple sequence alignment to a seqinr alignment object, calculate identity distances, and reconstruct a neighbor-joining phylogenetic tree.
input: HemoglobinAA.fasta (FASTA file containing hemoglobin amino acid sequences)
workflows.stages: 1. Read and align sequences ;; 2. Convert the alignment to seqinr format using msaConvert ;; 3. Compute a distance matrix using dist.alignment from seqinr ;; 4. Reconstruct a neighbor-joining tree using nj from ape ;; 5. Plot the phylogenetic tree
workflows.code:
hemoSeq <- readAAStringSet(system.file("examples/HemoglobinAA.fasta", package="msa"))
hemoAln <- msa(hemoSeq)
hemoAln2 <- msaConvert(hemoAln, type="seqinr::alignment")
library(seqinr)
d <- dist.alignment(hemoAln2, "identity")
library(ape)
hemoTree <- nj(d)
plot(hemoTree, main="Phylogenetic Tree of Hemoglobin Alpha Sequences")
